**WorldPainter layer files (experimental).** A custom layer exported from WorldPainter (Export in its menu, a `.layer` file) no longer has to be made again by hand: **Import WorldPainter layer…**, at the top of the Layers panel, reads several at once, and dropping them on the window does the same. Plant layers become ground covers with the same plants; custom object layers become object layers of their objects, Bo2 trees, schematics and structures read from the file, with their offset, frequency, random turn and density; ground covers become a ground cover of their blocks laid over the land, or a terrain of them where they take the place of the top of the land; underground pockets and combined layers (with the custom terrain written with them) become Massif's. A report says what each file became and what was not carried over: tunnel, floating and custom annotation layers, objects' collision, leaf decay and foundation settings, entities, a ground cover's edges and noise. Your map's own layers are never changed: a layer of the file with the name of one of yours comes in as a layer of its own. Also from `.world` files, old materials known only by their number (as in older custom terrains and ground covers) now come in as their block rather than as stone, and a custom object layer named like a tree of WorldPainter's tree pack keeps its own objects.
